author: V. I. Hancock
title: Queens County: Hispanic students made up largest ethnicity in 2024-25 school year
text:
Hispanic students were the most prevalent ethnic group among those enrolled in New York schools in the 2024-25 school year, according to the New York State Education Department .
Of the 249,911 students attending Queens County schools, 42.8% were Hispanic. Asian or Pacific Islander represented the second-largest ethnic group, making up 28.7% of Queens County students.
In the previous school year, Hispanic was also the most common student ethnicity in Queens County, representing 42.7% of the student body.
Scholars’ Academy had the most even distribution of races among county schools, with 28.9% white students, 27.8% Hispanic students, 18.9% Asian or Pacific Islander students, 18.6% Black students, 3% multiracial students, and 2.7% American Indian or Alaska Native students.
In the 2024-25 school year, the total number of students enrolled in public schools in the county dropped to 0.3% when compared to the previous year.
A recent study by Scholaroo ranked New York’s education system among the best in the U.S. , and placed it as the second best in terms of school quality.
Currently, the state has the highest per-pupil spending in the nation at $33,440 , or a total of $84.7 billion annually.
